commit: the commit that adds this entry
what: Search rounds changed from 60-epoch R1 (keep 3) -> R2 400 epochs (keep 2) -> R3 seed check, to coarse (8 shared draws + anchor) -> fine (8 draws around each cell's best coarse config) -> seed check (best 2 of coarse + fine get seed 1), every round trained to early stopping under the 400-epoch cap. Adds the "fine" block; removes the study60 protocol.
why: v1 tuning runs (504 runs, 150-epoch cap) peaked at a median epoch of 145 and 92 % after epoch 60, so a 60-epoch cut ranks learning speed, not final quality; coarse-to-fine random search chosen by the user.
runs_affected: all study v2 tuning runs (none had run)
results_seen: none: no study v2 run had started

commit: the commit that adds this entry
what: Three rule changes after the code review: (1) A0 = the cell winner with the best score on common targets, no 1-SE rule (the 1-SE rule still picks each cell's winner); (2) the D23 gate makes one comparison, against the shorter full-overlap length with the best R1 score, instead of against every shorter length; (3) each pre-registered comparison is scored on the samples both of its arms predict, replacing 'every arm from the latest first prediction of any final arm'; that shared start is kept for the descriptive scores and the val-test agreement (D2b). Adds 'limitations' (no shuffling vs overlap, fixed training settings, ridge lags, conservative rule). Considered and not adopted: drawing 1 or 2 layers in the fine round (fine draws keep the centre's layers).
why: (1) parameter count does not depend on window length, so the fewest-parameters tie-break ignored the setting being chosen and, with 6 people, many cells fall within 1 SE; (2) comparing against every shorter length made stopping more likely by multiplicity; (3) the old rule made F3's scored samples depend on F1's gate results and dropped up to 10 s of every trial from comparisons not involving long windows, while the descriptive curve and D2b need one shared sample set to line up. Layers stay fixed in the fine round because drawing them afresh would move most fine draws off the centre whose learning-rate and dropout ranges were narrowed, and the seed check already pools coarse and fine configs, so the other layer count stays in contention.
runs_affected: all study v2 runs (none had run)
results_seen: none: no study v2 run had started

commit: the commit that adds this entry
what: 6-day compute budget (user): coarse draws 8 -> 6 (+ anchor), fine draws 8 -> 4, final seeds per cell winner 5 -> 3 (A0, A2, A3 keep 10); 6 workers; only the 2 s window is screened and a pass is reported as 'not tuned (budget)' (5 s and 10 s are not screened); a run-time budget check, when the R1 runs of every cell but 75 % overlap end and again when R1 ends, adds, in order, drop the 75 % overlap cells (their R1 runs come after the first check), skip the 2 s check, fine draws 4 -> 2, until the projection is within 6 days (EXPERIMENTS/tuning/budget.py, results_v2/budget.json).
why: The full-budget design projected 8.2-8.7 days, and more if runs train past epoch 180; the user set a hard 6-day limit. The cuts keep every cell and every pre-registered comparison and were the shortening path listed in the plan. The fallback depends on run times only, never on scores. A lower epoch cap was considered as a fallback step and not adopted: applied mid-study it would give runs of the same round different training budgets. A 7th worker was not adopted (the M3 has 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores).
runs_affected: all study v2 runs (none had run)
results_seen: none: no study v2 run had started

commit: the commit that adds this entry
what: The torque target is now down-sampled (zero-phase FIR, scipy.signal.decimate) over the whole trial and then trimmed, instead of trimmed and then down-sampled (ML/research/data.py _process_active, CACHE_VERSION 1 -> 2). Applies to every non-legacy setting, including all study v2 settings (causal envelope, 1 s end trim); the legacy setting (zero-phase envelope, no end trim) keeps the original order and is unchanged. Inputs, angles, sample times and trial lengths are unchanged.
why: Found while checking why the last 1 s is trimmed: down-sampling after the trims put the filter's ~0.1 s edge effect at the new edges, so the first and last ~50 ms of every target were wrong (172 active trials: median 1.6 Nm, 95th percentile 9-49 Nm, in the edge 50 ms; zero from 100 ms on). Down-sampling first gives every kept target real torque on both sides, which is the reason the end trim is kept.
runs_affected: No study v2 run is re-run: all were trained and scored on the old targets. Re-scoring the saved session-2 predictions of every FE_* experiment against the corrected target (EXPERIMENTS/analysis/target_edge_rescore.py) changes 72 of ~70,000 scored samples per person and MAE by -0.022 % to +0.005 % (median -0.006 %), R2 by at most 0.00004, for every experiment and person. Training targets changed on the same ~0.1 % of session-1 samples; that effect was not measured. Runs from this commit on use the corrected target.
results_seen: all study v2 results, including session 2 (the fix concerns the target's construction, not any score or choice)

commit: the commit that adds this entry
what: Adds FE_A0_zerophase: A0 with a zero-phase envelope (forward-backward filters, 2nd-order 2 Hz low-pass as in A0), seeds 10-12, S1->S2 (A0's first 3 of its 10 seeds, user's choice to keep it under an hour). For this, the zero-phase envelope accepts lp_order (ML/preprocessing/emg_envelope.py extract_envelope, ML/research/data.py _envelope_fn); with lp_order 4 it is unchanged.
why: To measure what the causal (real-time) envelope costs against the offline zero-phase one, asked by the user. Descriptive only: not a pre-registered comparison, and it changes no choice or rule. The zero-phase envelope leads the causal one by 120-130 ms (CH, every active trial); sample times and torque targets are identical.
runs_affected: none of the existing runs; adds 18 runs
results_seen: all study v2 results, including session 2

what: Second fine round (R4) added as a precision check of the tuning: pre-registered in EXPERIMENTS/protocol/fine_round_2.json and run by EXPERIMENTS/tuning/fine2.py. Cells carry_2s, w50_full, w100_full: 4 new fine draws around each cell winner on seeds 0-2, plus seed 2 of the winner (TS2_R4_<cell>_w); 234 session-1 runs.
